g.text: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable
progress by combining vision encoders with large language models
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress by combining vision encoders with large language models (Liu et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023).

g.text: While recent work demonstrates that more detailed image captions
can improve visual understanding (Li et al., 2024), this intuition
g.title: N2 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) While recent work demonstrates that more detailed image captions can improve visual understanding (Li et al., 2024), this intuition does not always hold.

g.text: The Long-Caption Paradox describes the counterintuitive finding
that longer captions can hurt MLLM performance in certain training
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) The Long-Caption Paradox describes the counterintuitive finding that longer captions can hurt MLLM performance in certain training paradigms.

g.text: This paradox is particularly pronounced in ReVision-style
text-only pretraining (Yu et al., 2026), which enables MLLM
training without paired images by exploiting the modality gap in
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) This paradox is particularly pronounced in ReVision-style text-only pretraining (Yu et al., 2026), which enables MLLM training without paired images by exploiting the modality gap in contrastive embedding spaces.

g.text: ReVision aligns text to image stats
ReVision transforms text embeddings to match image embedding statistics,
allowing captions to serve as pseudo-visual inputs.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) ReVision transforms text embeddings to match image embedding statistics, allowing captions to serve as pseudo-visual inputs.

g.text: However, verbose captions introduce noise in the text embedding space that
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, verbose captions introduce noise in the text embedding space that disrupts the statistical alignment process.

g.text: C3 and Unicorn share long-text issue
Related approaches such as C3 (Zhang et al., 2024) and Unicorn (Yu
et al., 2025) face similar challenges when processing long-form
g.title: N7 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Related approaches such as C3 (Zhang et al., 2024) and Unicorn (Yu et al., 2025) face similar challenges when processing long-form text.

g.text: We hypothesize that CLIP-scored caption distillation—selecting the most
visually-relevant sentences from long captions based on image-text
similarity—could mitigate this paradox by preserving information density
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) We hypothesize that CLIP-scored caption distillation—selecting the most visually-relevant sentences from long captions based on image-text similarity—could mitigate this paradox by preserving information density while reducing length.

g.text: To test this hypothesis, we conduct a controlled micro-scale
experiment comparing three conditions: (A) original long captions,
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) To test this hypothesis, we conduct a controlled micro-scale experiment comparing three conditions: (A) original long captions, (B) random length-matched selection, and (C) CLIP-scored selection.

g.text: Our results show that the hypothesis is not supported: caption distillation
(51.88% mean accuracy) underperforms long captions (53.31%) by 1.43
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=0) Our results show that the hypothesis is not supported: caption distillation (51.88% mean accuracy) underperforms long captions (53.31%) by 1.43 percentage points.

g.text: However, content-aware selection consistently outperforms random selection
(49.90%) by 1.98 percentage points, validating that CLIP-based scoring
preserves more useful information than indiscriminate filtering.
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) However, content-aware selection consistently outperforms random selection (49.90%) by 1.98 percentage points, validating that CLIP-based scoring preserves more useful information than indiscriminate filtering.

g.text: The first systematic study of caption distillation for
ReVision-style text-only MLLM pretraining, providing a rigorous
test of whether content-aware sentence selection can mitigate the
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) The first systematic study of caption distillation for ReVision-style text-only MLLM pretraining, providing a rigorous test of whether content-aware sentence selection can mitigate the Long-Caption Paradox.

g.text: A negative result with mechanistic explanation: sentence-level
filtering inevitably loses object-presence mentions, as evidenced
by POPE recall dropping from 98% to 88%.
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) A negative result with mechanistic explanation: sentence-level filtering inevitably loses object-presence mentions, as evidenced by POPE recall dropping from 98% to 88%.

g.text: An actionable insight for future work: caption condensation
(rewriting to preserve information in fewer words) may succeed
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) An actionable insight for future work: caption condensation (rewriting to preserve information in fewer words) may succeed where filtering fails.
